Recyclable and Low Fat Products.title: Recyclable and Low Fat Products
Recyclable and Low Fat Products.problemStatement: Find the ids of products that are both low fat and recyclable.
Recyclable and Low Fat Products.schema: Create table If Not Exists Products (product_id int, low_fats ENUM('Y', 'N'), recyclable ENUM('Y', 'N'))

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT product_id FROM Products WHERE low_fats = 'Y' AND recyclable = 'Y';
solutions.explanation: Filters the Products table to return only those product IDs where both the low_fats and recyclable columns contain the value 'Y'.

edgeCases: No products are both low fat and recyclable.
All products are both low fat and recyclable.
The table is empty.

Find Customer Referee.title: Find Customer Referee
Find Customer Referee.problemStatement: Find the names of the customer that are not referred by the customer with id = 2.
Find Customer Referee.schema: Create table If Not Exists Customer (id int, name varchar(25), referee_id int)

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT name FROM Customer WHERE referee_id != 2 OR referee_id IS NULL;
solutions.explanation: Selects customer names where the referee_id is not equal to 2. An explicit check for 'IS NULL' is required because SQL three-valued logic evaluates comparisons with NULL (such as referee_id != 2) as UNKNOWN, which excludes NULLs from the result.

edgeCases: All customers have a referee_id equal to 2 (should return empty output).
The referee_id values are all NULL (should return all customers).
The referee_id is NULL for some customers and non-null (excluding 2) for others.

Big Countries.title: Big Countries
Big Countries.problemStatement: A country is big if it has an area of at least 3 million sq km, or it has a population of at least 25 million. Find the name, population, and area of the big countries.
Big Countries.schema: Create table If Not Exists World (name varchar(50), continent varchar(50), area int, population int, gdp bigint)

solutions.name: Optimal (OR)
solutions.query: SELECT name, population, area FROM World WHERE area >= 3000000 OR population >= 25000000;
solutions.explanation: Selects name, population, and area where either the area condition or the population condition is satisfied.

solutions.name: Better (UNION)
solutions.explanation: Uses UNION to merge results of two queries. This is often faster because SQL engines can leverage individual indexes on the 'area' and 'population' columns, whereas an OR query can force a full-table scan.

edgeCases: Countries matching only one criteria.
Countries matching both criteria.
Countries matching neither criteria.

Article Views I.title: Article Views I
Article Views I.problemStatement: Find all the authors that viewed at least one of their own articles. Return the result table sorted by id in ascending order.
Article Views I.schema: Create table If Not Exists Views (article_id int, author_id int, viewer_id int, view_date date)

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT DISTINCT author_id AS id FROM Views WHERE author_id = viewer_id ORDER BY id ASC;
solutions.explanation: Filters rows where the viewer and the author are the same person. DISTINCT is used to remove duplicates when an author views their own article multiple times. Results are ordered by id in ascending order.

edgeCases: Authors viewing their own articles multiple times (handled by DISTINCT).
No authors viewed their own articles.
The table is empty.

Invalid Tweets.title: Invalid Tweets
Invalid Tweets.problemStatement: Find the IDs of the invalid tweets. A tweet is invalid if the number of characters used in the content of the tweet is strictly greater than 15.
Invalid Tweets.schema: Create table If Not Exists Tweets (tweet_id int, content varchar(50))

rows: Let us make America great again!

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT tweet_id FROM Tweets WHERE CHAR_LENGTH(content) > 15;
solutions.explanation: Uses CHAR_LENGTH() to count characters in the tweet content and filters for tweets with lengths strictly greater than 15. Note that CHAR_LENGTH() is preferred over LENGTH() because LENGTH() returns the length in bytes, which can differ for multi-byte characters.

edgeCases: Tweets with content length exactly 15 (should not be included).
Tweets with empty content (length 0).
Content containing multi-byte characters like emojis or non-English script.

Product Sales Analysis I.title: Product Sales Analysis I
Product Sales Analysis I.problemStatement: Reports the product_name, year, and price for each sale_id in the Sales table.
Product Sales Analysis I.schema:
Create table If Not Exists Sales (sale_id int, product_id int, year int, quantity int, price int)
Create table If Not Exists Product (product_id int, product_name varchar(10))

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT p.product_name, s.year, s.price FROM Sales s INNER JOIN Product p ON s.product_id = p.product_id;
solutions.explanation: Joins the Sales table and Product table on the common field product_id to fetch the name of the product sold, the year of sale, and the price of the sale.

edgeCases: Products that exist in the Product table but have no matching entries in the Sales table (handled by INNER JOIN which omits them).
Multiple sales of the same product in the same year or in different years.

Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make An.title: Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make Any Transactions
Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make An.problemStatement: Find the IDs of the users who visited without making any transactions and the number of times they made these types of visits.
Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make An.schema:
Create table If Not Exists Visits (visit_id int, customer_id int)
Create table If Not Exists Transactions (transaction_id int, visit_id int, amount int)

solutions.name: Optimal (LEFT JOIN)
solutions.query: SELECT v.customer_id, COUNT(v.visit_id) AS count_no_trans FROM Visits v LEFT JOIN Transactions t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL GROUP BY v.customer_id;
solutions.explanation: Executes a LEFT JOIN between Visits and Transactions on visit_id. If a customer visited but made no transactions, all transaction columns will be NULL. We filter for these cases using 'WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL', group the results by customer_id, and count the occurrences.

solutions.name: Alternative (NOT IN)
solutions.query: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(visit_id) AS count_no_trans FROM Visits WHERE visit_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT visit_id FROM Transactions) GROUP BY customer_id;
solutions.explanation: Selects customer_ids and count of visits where the visit_id is not present in the Transactions table.

edgeCases: Multiple transactions made in a single visit (the LEFT JOIN approach ensures we count only visits without any transaction).
All customers made transactions (should return empty output).
No customer made transactions.

Rising Temperature.title: Rising Temperature
Rising Temperature.problemStatement: Find all dates' Id with higher temperatures compared to its previous dates (yesterday).
Rising Temperature.schema: Create table If Not Exists Weather (id int, recordDate date, temperature int)

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT w1.id FROM Weather w1 JOIN Weather w2 ON DATEDIFF(w1.recordDate, w2.recordDate) = 1 WHERE w1.temperature > w2.temperature;
solutions.explanation: Self-joins the Weather table to compare each day (w1) with the day immediately preceding it (w2, where DATEDIFF(w1.recordDate, w2.recordDate) = 1). The WHERE condition filters for days where w1's temperature is strictly greater than w2's temperature.

edgeCases: Non-consecutive dates in the database (e.g. gaps of a few days - DATEDIFF condition handles this and returns only consecutive day rises).
Equal temperatures on consecutive days (should not be included).
Temperature rises but dates are out of order in the database (handled properly by the join condition).

Average Time of Process per Machine.title: Average Time of Process per Machine
Average Time of Process per Machine.problemStatement: Find the average time each machine takes to complete a process. The average time is calculated by the total time to complete every process on the machine divided by the number of processes. Round processing_time to 3 decimal places.
Average Time of Process per Machine.schema: Create table If Not Exists Activity (machine_id int, process_id int, activity_type ENUM('start', 'end'), timestamp float)

solutions.name: Optimal (Self Join)
solutions.query: SELECT a1.machine_id, ROUND(AVG(a2.timestamp - a1.timestamp), 3) AS processing_time FROM Activity a1 JOIN Activity a2 ON a1.machine_id = a2.machine_id AND a1.process_id = a2.process_id AND a1.activity_type = 'start' AND a2.activity_type = 'end' GROUP BY a1.machine_id;
solutions.explanation: Self-joins the Activity table on machine_id and process_id to match the 'start' activity row (a1) with the 'end' activity row (a2). Calculates the difference between their timestamps and takes the average per machine, rounded to 3 decimal places.

solutions.name: Better (Conditional Aggregation)
solutions.query: SELECT machine_id, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN activity_type = 'end' THEN timestamp ELSE -timestamp END) / COUNT(DISTINCT process_id), 3) AS processing_time FROM Activity GROUP BY machine_id;
solutions.explanation: Sums the timestamps by adding 'end' activity timestamps and subtracting 'start' activity timestamps, then divides the sum by the count of distinct process IDs for each machine.

edgeCases: Varying number of processes per machine.
Timestamps with high precision float values (handled by ROUND).

Employee Bonus.title: Employee Bonus
Employee Bonus.problemStatement: Report the name and bonus amount of each employee with a bonus less than 1000.
Employee Bonus.schema:
Create table If Not Exists Employee (empId int, name varchar(255), supervisor int, salary int)
Create table If Not Exists Bonus (empId int, bonus int)

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT e.name, b.bonus FROM Employee e LEFT JOIN Bonus b ON e.empId = b.empId WHERE b.bonus < 1000 OR b.bonus IS NULL;
solutions.explanation: Performs a LEFT JOIN to keep all employees regardless of whether they have a bonus record. The WHERE filter keeps only records where the bonus is strictly less than 1000, or where the bonus is NULL (meaning they received no bonus).

edgeCases: Employees who do not have a record in the Bonus table (their bonus is NULL, which must be included).
Employees with a bonus of exactly 1000 (should be excluded).
All employees have bonuses >= 1000.

Students and Examinations.title: Students and Examinations
Students and Examinations.problemStatement: Find the number of times each student attended each exam. Return the result table ordered by student_id and subject_name.
Students and Examinations.schema:
Create table If Not Exists Students (student_id int, student_name varchar(20))
Create table If Not Exists Subjects (subject_name varchar(20))
Create table If Not Exists Examinations (student_id int, subject_name varchar(20))

solutions.name: Optimal (CROSS JOIN + LEFT JOIN)
solutions.query: SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, sub.subject_name, COUNT(e.subject_name) AS attended_exams FROM Students s CROSS JOIN Subjects sub LEFT JOIN Examinations e ON s.student_id = e.student_id AND sub.subject_name = e.subject_name GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name, sub.subject_name ORDER BY s.student_id, sub.subject_name;
solutions.explanation: Generates a full grid of all student-subject pairs using a CROSS JOIN. Then, LEFT JOINs the Examinations table to count actual exams attended for each pair. Grouping by student and subject and counting e.subject_name ensures that pairs with no exams correctly display a count of 0.

edgeCases: Students who have not attended any exams (attended_exams should show 0 for all subjects).
Subjects that no student has taken.
Ensuring proper ordering of output by student_id and subject_name.

Managers with at Least 5 Direct Reports.title: Managers with at Least 5 Direct Reports
Managers with at Least 5 Direct Reports.problemStatement: Find the managers with at least five direct reports.
Managers with at Least 5 Direct Reports.schema: Create table If Not Exists Employee (id int, name varchar(255), department varchar(255), managerId int)

solutions.name: Optimal (Subquery IN)
solutions.query: SELECT name FROM Employee WHERE id IN (SELECT managerId FROM Employee GROUP BY managerId HAVING COUNT(id) >= 5);
solutions.explanation: Selects employee names whose IDs are in the list of managerIds that have 5 or more reports. The subquery groups the Employee table by managerId and counts the reports.

solutions.name: Alternative (Self Join)
solutions.query: SELECT e1.name FROM Employee e1 JOIN Employee e2 ON e1.id = e2.managerId GROUP BY e1.id, e1.name HAVING COUNT(e2.id) >= 5;
solutions.explanation: Self-joins the Employee table to match managers (e1) with their subordinates (e2). Groups by the manager's ID and name, and filters using HAVING COUNT(e2.id) >= 5.

edgeCases: A manager has exactly 5 direct reports.
A manager has fewer than 5 direct reports (should not be included).
An employee is their own manager (if cycle exists, but standard constraint avoids this).

Confirmation Rate.title: Confirmation Rate
Confirmation Rate.problemStatement: Find the confirmation rate of each user. The confirmation rate is the number of 'confirmed' messages divided by the total number of requested confirmation messages. Users with no requests should have a rate of 0. Round to 2 decimal places.
Confirmation Rate.schema:
Create table If Not Exists Signups (user_id int, time_stamp datetime)
Create table If Not Exists Confirmations (user_id int, time_stamp datetime, action ENUM('confirmed', 'timeout'))

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT s.user_id, ROUND(IFNULL(AVG(c.action = 'confirmed'), 0), 2) AS confirmation_rate FROM Signups s LEFT JOIN Confirmations c ON s.user_id = c.user_id GROUP BY s.user_id;
solutions.explanation: Uses a LEFT JOIN to ensure all registered users are represented. The conditional expression `c.action = 'confirmed'` evaluates to 1 for confirmed requests and 0 for timeouts. The AVG function computes the confirmation rate. IFNULL sets the rate to 0 for users with no confirmation requests, and ROUND limits the result to 2 decimal places.

edgeCases: User has signed up but has zero confirmation requests (handled by IFNULL to return 0.00).
User has only 'timeout' actions (rate is 0.00).
User has only 'confirmed' actions (rate is 1.00).

Not Boring Movies.title: Not Boring Movies
Not Boring Movies.problemStatement: Find movies with an odd numbered ID and a description that is not 'boring'. Return the result table ordered by rating in descending order.
Not Boring Movies.schema: Create table If Not Exists Cinema (id int, movie varchar(255), description varchar(255), rating float)

solutions.name: Optimal
solutions.query: SELECT id, movie, description, rating FROM Cinema WHERE id % 2 = 1 AND description != 'boring' ORDER BY rating DESC;
solutions.explanation: Selects all fields where the id is odd (evaluated using modulo operator `id % 2 = 1`) and the description is not 'boring'. Finally, orders the records by rating in descending order.

edgeCases: Movies with even IDs and non-boring descriptions (should be excluded).
Movies with odd IDs and boring descriptions (should be excluded).
All movies are boring or have even IDs (should return empty result).

Average Selling Price.title: Average Selling Price
Average Selling Price.problemStatement: Find the average selling price for each product. average_price should be rounded to 2 decimal places. If a product does not have any sales, its average selling price is 0.
Average Selling Price.schema:
Create table If Not Exists Prices (product_id int, start_date date, end_date date, price int)
Create table If Not Exists UnitsSold (product_id int, purchase_date date, units int)

solutions.name: Optimal (LEFT JOIN + SUM)
solutions.query: SELECT p.product_id, ROUND(IFNULL(SUM(u.units * p.price) / SUM(u.units), 0), 2) AS average_price FROM Prices p LEFT JOIN UnitsSold u ON p.product_id = u.product_id AND u.purchase_date BETWEEN p.start_date AND p.end_date GROUP BY p.product_id;
solutions.explanation: LEFT JOINs Prices and UnitsSold on the product ID and matches the purchase_date between the product price start and end dates. Groups by product_id to compute the total revenue (SUM of units * price) divided by total units sold. IFNULL handles products with no sales, defaulting their average price to 0, and ROUND formats the output to two decimal places.

edgeCases: A product in Prices has no sales records in UnitsSold (should return average_price 0.00).
The purchase date falls exactly on the start_date or end_date (handled correctly by BETWEEN which is inclusive).
